concepts.name: Mimamsa: Foundational Nature and Classification within Astika Schools
key_dimensions: Distinction between Purva Mimamsa (Mimamsa) and Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) — same root, divergent focus
Why Mimamsa is classified as Astika despite minimal focus on God/liberation
Mimamsa's acceptance of Vedic authority (Shruti) as the supreme epistemological source
UPSC trap: Mimamsa vs. Charvaka — both skeptical of theism but diametrically opposite on Vedic authority

concepts.name: Jaimini and the Mimamsa Sutras: Dharma as the Central Inquiry
key_dimensions: Jaimini's Mimamsa Sutras as the foundational text — 'atha-ato dharma jijnasa' (inquiry into dharma)
Dharma defined through Vedic injunctions (vidhi) rather than metaphysical speculation
Role of Shabara Bhashya as the primary commentary on Mimamsa Sutras
UPSC trap: Confusing Jaimini (Mimamsa) with Badarayana/Vyasa (Vedanta Sutras/Brahma Sutras)

concepts.name: Mimamsa Epistemology: Pramanas (Sources of Valid Knowledge)
key_dimensions: Mimamsa accepts six pramanas: Pratyaksha, Anumana, Upamana, Shabda, Arthapatti, Anupalabdhi
Anupalabdhi (non-apprehension) as Mimamsa's unique contribution — distinguishes it from other schools
Shabda (verbal testimony) elevated to the highest pramana, specifically Vedic Shabda
UPSC trap: Nyaya accepts 4 pramanas, Samkhya accepts 3 — comparative question on pramanas across schools

concepts.name: Theory of Shabda Nitya: Eternal and Uncreated Nature of the Vedas
key_dimensions: Mimamsa's doctrine that Vedic words (Shabda) are eternal, self-valid, and authorless (Apaurusheya)
Distinction between Sphota theory (Grammarians/Vyakarana) and Mimamsa's rejection of Sphota
Self-validity of Vedic knowledge (Svatah Pramanya) — knowledge is valid unless proven otherwise
UPSC trap: Apaurusheya applied to Vedas — contrast with Nyaya which accepts God as author of Vedas

concepts.name: Mimamsa Theory of Karma and Apurva: Ritual Action and Unseen Force
key_dimensions: Apurva — the unseen potency generated by correct Vedic rituals that bridges action and future result
Mimamsa's justification for why rituals prescribed in Vedas must produce results even without immediate effects
Karma in Mimamsa is ritualistic (Karma-kanda) — not ethical karma of Vedanta/Buddhism
UPSC trap: Apurva is unique to Mimamsa — not found in Nyaya-Vaisheshika or Vedanta systems

concepts.name: Mimamsa on Moksha and the Soul (Atman): A Contrarian View
key_dimensions: Early Mimamsa (Kumarila, Prabhakara) does not treat Moksha as the primary goal — Svarga (heaven) through ritual is central
Atman in Mimamsa is eternal, multiple, and distinct for each individual — pluralistic ontology
Later Mimamsa reconciliation with Moksha as cessation of rebirth (not blissful union with Brahman)
UPSC trap: Mimamsa Atman (plural, agent of ritual) vs. Advaita Vedanta Atman (singular, identical to Brahman)

concepts.name: Kumarila Bhatta vs. Prabhakara: Two Sub-Schools of Mimamsa
key_dimensions: Kumarila Bhatta (Bhatta school) — upheld Svatah Pramanya and defended Vedic rituals against Buddhist critique
Prabhakara (Prabhakara school / Guru-mata) — theory of 'Triputipratyaksha' (threefold self-luminous cognition)
Key difference: Theory of Error — Kumarila's Viparita Khyati vs. Prabhakara's Akhyati
UPSC trap: Both are Mimamsa sub-schools but differ on perception, error, and the self — often confused

concepts.name: Badarayana and the Brahma Sutras: Foundation of Vedanta
key_dimensions: Brahma Sutras (Vedanta Sutras / Shariraka Mimamsa) — systematic inquiry into Brahman
'Janmadyasya yatah' — Brahman as the source, sustainer, and dissolver of the universe (first Sutra's meaning)
Brahma Sutras as one of the three canonical texts (Prasthanatrayi) of Vedanta alongside Upanishads and Bhagavad Gita
UPSC trap: Prasthanatrayi — all three Vedanta schools (Advaita, Vishishtadvaita, Dvaita) accept the same texts but interpret them differently

concepts.name: Advaita Vedanta of Adi Shankaracharya: Core Metaphysics
key_dimensions: Brahman as the only reality (non-dual) — Nirguna Brahman (without attributes) as ultimate truth
Maya — the cosmic illusion that makes Brahman appear as the phenomenal world; neither real nor unreal (Anirvacaniya)
Vivartavada — the world is an apparent transformation (vivarta) of Brahman, not a real one
UPSC trap: Vivartavada (Advaita) vs. Parinamavada (Samkhya and Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita) — fundamental ontological distinction

concepts.name: Shankaracharya's Two Levels of Truth: Vyavaharika and Paramarthika
key_dimensions: Paramarthika Satta (absolute reality) — only Brahman exists; Vyavaharika Satta (empirical reality) — world is practically real
Pratibhasika Satta (illusory reality) — example of snake-rope illusion (Rajju-sarpa nyaya)
How Advaita reconciles Vedic rituals and devotion at empirical level while asserting non-dualism at absolute level
UPSC trap: Advaita does not deny empirical world's utility — it only denies its ultimate reality; often mischaracterized as nihilism

concepts.name: Shankaracharya's Doctrine of Avidya (Ignorance) and Moksha
key_dimensions: Avidya (ignorance) as the root cause of bondage — superimposition (Adhyasa) of non-self onto Atman
Jnana (knowledge of identity of Atman and Brahman) as the only path to Moksha — Jnana Marga supremacy
Jivanmukti — liberation while still living in a body, unique to Advaita
UPSC trap: Shankaracharya's critique of Mimamsa (karma alone cannot give Moksha) and Samkhya — important for philosophical debates

concepts.name: Vishishtadvaita of Ramanujacharya: Qualified Non-Dualism
key_dimensions: Brahman as Saguna (with attributes) — identified with Vishnu/Narayana; Chit (souls) and Achit (matter) are real but form the 'body' of Brahman
Rejection of Maya as illusion — the world and individual souls are real modifications (Parinamavada) of Brahman
Bhakti as the supreme path to Moksha — Prapatti (surrender) to God; critique of Advaita's Jnana-only path
UPSC trap: Ramanujacharya's Sri Bhashya is a commentary on Brahma Sutras directly refuting Shankaracharya — same text, opposite conclusions

concepts.name: Dvaita Vedanta of Madhvacharya: Pure Dualism
key_dimensions: Five fundamental distinctions (Pancha Bheda): God-soul, God-matter, soul-soul, soul-matter, matter-matter
Vishnu/Brahman as completely independent (Svatantra); souls and world as eternally dependent (Paratantra)
Madhvacharya's unique doctrine of eternal damnation for some souls (Tamo-yogya) — no universal liberation
UPSC trap: Dvaita vs. Advaita vs. Vishishtadvaita — all three use Prasthanatrayi but arrive at contradictory metaphysical conclusions

concepts.name: Comparative Analysis: Advaita, Vishishtadvaita, and Dvaita on Key Issues
key_dimensions: Nature of Brahman: Nirguna (Advaita) vs. Saguna-Vishnu (Vishishtadvaita, Dvaita)
Status of the world: Vivarta/Illusion (Advaita) vs. Real transformation (Vishishtadvaita, Dvaita)
Path to Moksha: Jnana (Advaita) vs. Bhakti+Prapatti (Vishishtadvaita) vs. Grace of Vishnu (Dvaita)
UPSC trap: All three are Vedanta schools — but UPSC often asks which school rejects Maya most strongly (Dvaita rejects it entirely)

concepts.name: Mimamsa-Vedanta Relationship: Karma-Kanda vs. Jnana-Kanda
key_dimensions: Vedas divided into Karma-Kanda (ritual portion — basis of Mimamsa) and Jnana-Kanda/Upanishadic portion (basis of Vedanta)
Shankaracharya's argument that Jnana-Kanda supersedes Karma-Kanda for ultimate liberation
Mimamsa-Vedanta Samanvaya (synthesis) — some thinkers like Mandana Mishra tried to reconcile both
UPSC trap: Vedanta literally means 'end of the Vedas' (Veda + Anta) referring to Upanishads — not a rejection of Vedas

concepts.name: Shankaracharya's Socio-Religious Contributions: Beyond Philosophy
key_dimensions: Establishment of four Mathas (Sringeri, Dwaraka, Puri, Jyotirmath) to consolidate Hindu philosophical tradition
Dashanami Sampradaya — organization of Shaivite monastic orders under ten names
Shankaracharya's role in countering Buddhist influence in India — 'crypto-Buddhist' allegation by critics
UPSC trap: Shankaracharya's Smarta tradition — worship of five deities (Panchayatana Puja) as a syncretic practice

concepts.name: Vedanta and the Upanishads: Mahavakyas as Philosophical Cornerstones
key_dimensions: Four Mahavakyas from four Vedas: 'Prajnanam Brahma' (Aitareya), 'Aham Brahmasmi' (Brihadaranyaka), 'Tat Tvam Asi' (Chandogya), 'Ayam Atma Brahma' (Mandukya)
Advaita interpretation of 'Tat Tvam Asi' — identity of individual soul and Brahman
Vishishtadvaita reinterpretation — 'Tat Tvam Asi' means soul is a mode/attribute of Brahman, not identical
UPSC trap: Each Mahavakya is associated with a specific Veda and Upanishad — frequently asked factual question

concepts.name: Theory of Knowledge/Error in Vedanta: Adhyasa and Viveka
key_dimensions: Adhyasa (superimposition) — Shankaracharya's theory that we wrongly superimpose the self onto the body and vice versa
Viveka (discrimination) between Atman and Anatman as the first step toward liberation in Advaita
Difference between Advaita's Anirvacaniya Khyati (theory of error) and other schools' theories of error
UPSC trap: Advaita's theory of error (Anirvacaniya Khyati) vs. Nyaya's Anyatha Khyati vs. Mimamsa's Viparita Khyati — comparative trap question

concepts.name: Later Vedanta Schools: Bhedabheda, Shuddhadvaita, and Achintya Bhedabheda
key_dimensions: Bhedabheda (difference and non-difference) — Nimbarka: Brahman and souls are both identical and different simultaneously
Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism) of Vallabhacharya — Brahman as Krishna; world is real and pure (not Maya)
Achintya Bhedabheda of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu — inconceivable simultaneous difference and non-difference between Krishna and souls
UPSC trap: Multiple 'non-dualist' schools exist — Advaita, Shuddhadvaita, Achintya Bhedabheda all claim non-dualism but differ fundamentally

concepts.name: Mimamsa and Vedanta's Influence on Indian Legal and Social Traditions
key_dimensions: Mimamsa's hermeneutical principles used in interpreting Dharmashastra texts — influenced classical Hindu law (e.g., Mitakshara school)
Vedanta's influence on Neo-Vedanta reformers — Swami Vivekananda's Practical Vedanta and social reform agenda
Influence on Indian Constitution debates — Ambedkar's critique of Vedanta's social implications vs. its philosophical universalism
UPSC trap: Mimamsa principles of textual interpretation (like 'Uha' and 'Badha') were adopted in legal reasoning — cross-disciplinary relevance
